body:
Right now a cancelled task can't come back. Final columns have no actions (`board.rs` refuses a workflow that gives them any), and other edits there are refused with `E7004`. Add a way for the human to return a **cancelled** task to the backlog.

- The board's task details get a **Back to backlog** action, available only in `cancelled`. Decide whether this is a workflow action on the cancelled column (D-51 forbids actions in final columns, so that would need a decision), or a dedicated request like `POST /tasks/{id}/restore`. Record the choice in DECISIONS.md.
- The task keeps its title, body, notes, runs, links and `dependsOn`. If it was archived, it is unarchived (`archivedTime` cleared, D-95). `closedTime` stays, as D-87 says.
- Cancelling has already settled the task's changes, so there's nothing to undo. The next run starts fresh.
- Leaving the final column makes any task that depends on this one unfinished again, so those cards dim again (feature 29f4838ffb0cb0d0).
- Add a note to the task recording that the human brought it back.
- `complete` tasks stay as they are; this only applies to `cancelled`.
- Update Spec 15 and the board README, and add tests (Rust and `board_acceptance.py`): restore from cancelled, refuse from any other column, and unarchive.
title: Move a cancelled task back to the backlog
